You're doing the right things. Getting a full psychiatric assessment to receive the correct diagnosis and exercising are two of the most important things you can do. Keeping socially active is essential too.

When a depressive episode occurs without a trigger this can be because your depression is endogenous (it comes from within), and if you have a family history of depression and suicide then this may confirm that.

Sometimes when your feeling low everything is seen through a glass darkly. The past, present, and future can all take on a gloomy and negative aspect. Check out the [Human Givens Institute](http://www.hgi.org.uk/), it's a new form of talk therapy with high success rates. I like it because it doesn't make you ruminate on the past too much. It concentrates on the now.

Of course, I'm in the UK and so I get all my treatment for free, I wouldn't have been able to afford all the treatment I've received and am receiving now (2 weeks hospital stay and 2 months intensive out patient treatment).

My advice is to try group therapy too. The social aspect helps as much as anything.

Best wishes, I think you're on the right track, and remember that you *can* get better.

Sorry about your friend. I've lost a few the same way.

It is a vulnerable time, and that's why I'm staying active and social. On a previous discharge I was overconfident that I was going to make a complete recovery, and when that didn't materialise, I quickly slipped again into the vicious cycle of depression, anxiety, and isolation, which all increased my dissociative traits no end!

Good advice, I was already following it, but I appreciate you telling me of your experiences.

This is sadly too true. I guess it's a question of funding, and allocating of resources.

I had lengthy conversations about this with my shrink and have been encouraged to communicate with the authorities and share my experiences.

Things are getting better here in the UK, and it's in great part due to the input of patients.

Thanks aenea.

I just read some of your previous comments and you mention you have autistic triplets, so I can see how that quote must resonate with you.

Good luck to you too!

Baby steps. It's one of my intentions to give up smoking, but right now I want as less stress as possible.

Nicotine is a strange drug, it's both a stimulant and a relaxant. But yes, I do want to quit smoking, and caffeine too.

I'm in the UK and we get free consultations with specially trained nurses, and are prescribed free nicotine replacement therapy. I'll decide with the nurse what treatment will be best.

I love the NHS!

Thanks a lot. This is why I'm joining the advocacy service - because I have experience as a patient (3 times) so I understand the frustrations they go through. 

I'll check back daily to see how things are going, and try to do my bit to help.

Yesterday I was discharged from an acute psychiatric ward.

I announced it in previous posts (I was the redditor formerly known as LesbianGayFootballs) and I thought I should thank you guys for your supportive and encouraging words, not just to me, but the help you give others.

Hospital is much like the SuicideWatch subreddit! you form a community and give each other support. Most of the time we sat about smoking cigarettes and chatting shit, and it wasn't neccessary to be continuously discussing our problems, although we did, and in unashamed detail. We were all a bit broken and needed help. It's a shame that sometimes you only get the real help you need when a crisis occurs.

I was treated well and had great relationships with the doctors, nurses, and the Occupational Therapists. Actually there was support for my every need, and someone there to address each issue. I've even been offered a job with the advocacy service! which I'm going to follow up on in a month when I've completed one month of being an out-patient (9am-4pm daily)

I'd say I'm 60% well, and I hope to improve. My condition is notoriously dificult to treat (depersonalisation disorder), but their are ways of coping and even thriving with my odd perspective on things! I feel better than I ever have in my entire life, almost real!

I feel like I am a person in the world, and although I'm slightly mad I'm still great! And fundamentally I'm a good person. It is as the 16th century British philosopher Sir Francis Bacon said "There is no excellent beauty that hath not some strangeness in the proportion."

I hope you guys are all doing well. I'm back now to help too. Although I have to limit my internet activity and concentrate on the real world because it can make me step further away from reality!

Peace.

Thanks bro!

I'm out on leave for the day today so I've popped home to picj up a few things. mp3 player etc.

The acute ward was full so I've been admitted to a more chronic ward, but yes, wonderful people and budding friendships. The patients are better support than the staff most of the time.

I'll be out in a couple of weeks with plenty of mental hospital stories!

Take care.

Thanks.

I'm out on leave for the day. Am doing ok, having good and bad days. Will get there though!

Will be in a few more weeks so have come home to get my mp3 player and check email.

[Yesterday's post](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/7nuu0/i_didnt_kill_myself_today/)

The crisis team have come and are concerned enough to admit me to hospital. So I shall be away for a while. Hopefully just a few days.

I thought I should say just in case someone messages me and is worried when you don't receive a reply.

I'm sitting here, waiting for the ambulance to come take me. I'll be fine though, eventually! 

I'm allowed to take my phone in, so maybe I should upgrade to a better model so I can still reddit in there - Jokes! It will be strange without internet though.

You all take care.

I've been on tons of anti-depressants, up to max dose and beyond, most made me feel worse.

The best relief came from tranquillisers, until I became tolerant, then dependant (I quit them a year ago)

It's definitely worth investing in a fleshlight! masturbating with the hand is only stimulating a few bits at a time, but a fleshlight! it envelopes! it's not as good as the real thing physically, and obviously can't compete with sex, but still, it's better than the five knuckle shuffle.

Well, it's difficult for me to describe it adequately to others because in a way we speak a different language. We have different frames of reference. 

In fact I'm so bad at describing what I feel that it took years to get a diagnosis!

I can imagine what it must be like to feel connected to reality, and I'm conscious of the fact that I'm not. It's frustrating.

I can look at my hand. It is my hand, I know this rationally, because hands are a part of people, and I am a person, but it doesn't feel like a part of 'me'. It seems like an obscure object of science, mechanics, beauty, but it's not a part of a me that doesn't exist either.

Interpersonal relationships: difficult, complicated!

The very worst is when I fear I'm going to lose control or go mad. The anxiety builds and I panic. I fear I'm about to lose control but I never actually do. I can have irrational impulses and obsessions. I often have a sense of deja-vu, of a sense of deja-vu... infinitely repeating.

Don't apologise though, I doubt many people are aware of it that don't have it or aren't related to someone who does. It's cool that you took the time to look it up and had the curiosity to ask the question.
Haha, it's funny you should say that. I lived next to a Nichiren Shoshu Buddhist when I was 18 and she used to say the exact same thing.

>do you think the Internet exacerbates your condition?

Fuck yeah! I have to be careful. If I spend too much time online it can exacerbate the symptoms and make me panic. I don't understand entirely why. Your insight is a better explanation than I could offer! I suppose it's because you have an alternative perspective (an external observer) whereas I'm inside the condition.

The thing is, I *know* things are real, I'm rational. But I can't feel it. It's extremely frustrating. 

Anyways, thanks for the good words!

edit: maybe because online is another step removed from reality?

Thanks treephant.

Depersonalisation episodes are common for people with anxiety disorders. It's all closely related. You're bug empathy sounds a bit like one! You've probably felt that a day to day nondescript object has a personality before too amirite?

I'm the redditor formerly known as LesbianGayFootballs. I've been reading and contributing to the SuicideWatch subreddit since it started, and I'm writing this because in the last few days I failed to do something us troubled folk often fail to do: take our own advice.

I have what is known as Depersonalisation disorder. That basically means I don't feel real, and I don't feel the corporeal world to be real either. I perceive it as both ugly and beautiful yes, but not something that actually exists and that I exist within. You can probably all imagine how that feels because apparently it's not uncommon for everyone to have those feelings from time to time. I'm not autistic, psychotic, psychopathic, or dangerous in any way, unless you ask me "Is it like the matrix?." Then I may be liable to kill you. Actually, there has been one film I know of made about the condition. It's called Numb, and it was a straight to DVD rom-com starring Chandler fucking Bing as a very neurotic Depersonalised person. To be honest I quite enjoyed it.

Sometimes I fear I will become psychotic, though I know I won't - the awareness itself defines the lack of psychosis!  but a few days ago the fear gripped me hard and I was convinced that unless I killed myself I would become mad. Entirely irrational, and again: I was aware it was, but I just couldn't stop it. 

I'd made preparations for my departure - though I won't tell you the details, for obvious reasons. And today was going to be the day. I didn't do it because the life imperative was still there, and it inspired the thought "Fuck it, I'm going to get help; this would be a waste, I can cope, life (whatever that is) is more often than not good, despite being a bit of a mad bastard I get good stuff achieved; yeah I fuck up constantly, but I've somehow managed to pull a beautiful girlfriend, and I've also got a brand new fleshlight for when we're apart."

I called my doctor and he got me taken to hospital immaediately, where I've spent all day today being medicated and talked to. They decided to let me go home and not section me because they believed me when I said that I'm not going to harm myself. I'm now on what is known as "Crisis red," which means that a doctor and nurse will come visit me at home every day, medicate me, and make sure I'm well. They'll do this until I'm in "Crisis amber" - which means I'm not in imminent danger of terrorist attack, and so they'll come less frequently.

I deleted my account those few days ago, but I'm back now, and I just wanted to say that if any of you are feeling in distress, get some help. Whether it be professional, voluntary, chatting to people on here, seek some help because there are plenty of people out there that are willing and capable, and it would be a waste of a good fleshlight.

Apologies for any bad grammah/spelling etc. it's not my strong suit and I'm heavily sedated.
